Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Large radial tear of the posterior root with severe extrusion. Degenerative signal in the posterior horn and body. 
Medial compartment cartilage: Broad areas of high grade cartilage loss at the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low grade cartilage loss at the central lateral tibial plateau. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High grade fissuring at the medial and lateral patellar facets. Cartilage heterogeneity at the central trochlea. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 9 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Large radial tear of the posterior root of the medial meniscus with severe extrusion.
2.	Moderate tricompartmental chondrosis, most advanced in the medial compartment.
3.	Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for several months.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Mild reactive subchondral bone marrow edema at the weightbearing aspect of the medial compartment near the medial joint line. Medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartment marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Moderate Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant radial component at the posterior horn. Superior displacement of a meniscal flap at the posterior horn. Displacement of a meniscal flap into the tibiomeniscal recess. Severe meniscal body extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade articular cartilage loss of the weightbearing aspect of the joint with confluent areas of full-thickness cartilage loss at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity and diffuse low grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with areas of high-grade fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Confluent full-thickness cartilage loss throughout the patella with subchondral signal changes. Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss of the trochlea with regions of full-thickness loss.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No lateral patellar tilt. Mild lateral patellar translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 18 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Severe patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment osteoarthritis. Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant radial component at the posterior horn. Superior displacement of a small meniscal flap at the posterior horn-root junction. Severe meniscal extrusion.
2.	Moderate knee joint effusion. Moderate leaking Baker's cyst.

Findings:  There is a mild - moderate knee effusion. There is incomplete tearing of the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Mild extrusion of the medial meniscus from the joint is demonstrated. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage with mild osteophyte formation. Normal lateral compartment articular cartilage. There is severe thinning and loss of the caudal two-thirds of the patellar articular cartilage. The trochlear articular cartilage is relatively preserved.  
Conclusion: Incomplete tearing of the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Mild medial compartment and severe patellar articular cartilage degeneration.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 2 months which began after a twisting injury. [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental osteophytosis. Protuberant osteophytes extending into the femoral intercondylar notch. Inferior patellar enthesophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Small multiloculated leaking Baker's cyst with synovitis. 6 x 4 mm intra-articular body in the Baker's cyst. Fluid extends into the region of the pes anserinus 3 x 3 mm ossific intra-articular body at the anterolateral joint recess.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Intact.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing and posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle with areas of high-grade cartilage loss and full-thickness fissuring. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Horizontal oblique undersurface tear at the posterior horn-body junction.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage loss at the posterior lateral femoral condyle with areas of full-thickness fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity at the patella and trochlea with large confluent regions of full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial patellar facet and full-thickness fissuring throughout the trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Mild proximal patellar tendinosis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 16 mm, top-normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. Fluid tracking into the popliteus muscle sheath.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Deep soft tissue edema at the posterior distal thigh. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, worst at the patellofemoral compartment, where it is severe. Moderate knee joint effusion. Small multiloculated leaking Baker's cyst with synovitis. Intra-articular bodies at the anterolateral joint recess and in the Baker's cyst.
2.	Horizontal oblique undersurface tear at the lateral meniscus posterior horn-body junction.
3.	Joint fluid decompression into the popliteus muscle sheath with synovitis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain
Comparison: MRI right knee to [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No significant joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage thinning at the periphery of the medial femoral condyle medial tibial plateau. No full-thickness cartilage defect.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage thinning at the posterior lateral tibial plateau. No full-thickness defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Broad areas of full-thickness cartilage loss extending from the median ridge through the lateral patellar facet with subchondral cystic change. Broad areas of full-thickness cartilage loss along the lateral trochlea with subchondral cystic change. Cartilage heterogeneity and partial-thickness loss along the medial patellar facet and medial trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Medial collateral ligament is intact and normal in appearance. There is a mild MCL bursitis, significantly improved since prior study.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Trace edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Grade 4 patellofemoral compartment chondrosis, mildly progressed along the trochlea since prior study.
2. Mild MCL bursitis, significantly improved since prior study.
3. No meniscal tear or ligamentous injury.

Primjeren je intenzitet signala prikazanog dijela femura, tibije i fibule. Rubne koštane apozicije u
sklopu osteoartroze FT i FP zgloba.
Gotovo potpuni gubitak hrskavice u medijalnom dijelu tibiofemoralnog zglobnog prostora koji je
reducirane širine zglobnog prostora. Hondromalacija III stupnja u lateralnom dijelu.
Umjereni izljev u zglobu.
Prednji križni ligament urednog je signala te se prati u kontinuitetu.
Stražnji križni ligament urednog je signala te se prati u kontinuitetu.
Medijalni menisk: kompleksna ruptura na prijelazu stražnjeg roga u trup meniska s horizontalnom
komponentnom koja se širi u stražnji rog. Trup je meniska degeneriran i u cijelosti ekstrudiran
izvan zglobnog prostora. Blaža mukoidna degeneracija prednjeg i stražnjeg roga.
Lateralni menisk: blaža mukoidna degeneracija prednjeg i stražnjeg roga. Moguća manja
degenerativna ruptura prednjeg roga s gornje artikulacijske strane.
Lateralni i medijalni kolateralni ligamenti urednog su signala te se prate u kontinuitetu.
Blaža tendinoza pri hvatištu lig. patele. Tetiva kvadricepsa pri hvatištu zadebljana i povišenog
intenziteta signala u smislu tendinoze.
Sitna poplitealna cista, oko 13 mm u kraniokaudalnom promjeru.
Nekoliko manjih parameniscealnih cista uz stražnji rog lateralnog meniska ili zavlačenje
intraartikularnog izljeva.
Uredna je kongruencija zglobnih tijela femoropatelarnog zgloba. Izrazito stanjena hrskavica
lateralne fasete patele te potpuni gubitak hrskavice medijalne fasete sa zonama subhondralne
cistične degeneracije - hondromalacija IV stupnja.
Lamele slobodne tekućine u mekim tkivima.

Opsežne gonartrotske promjene uz vidljivu kompletnu rupturu prednje križne sveze u srednjoj
trećini. Održana je stražnja križna sveza.
Kosa ruptura stražnjeg roga lateralnog meniska na prijelazu prema stražnjem korijenu.
Kompleksna ruptura trupa i stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska sa ekstruzijom i flapom meniska
pod medijalni kolateralni ligament prema kaudalno te polilobuliranim ganglion cistama
parameniscealno.
Kolateralni ligamenti su održani, lateralni blaže degenerativno promijenjen, medijalni distendiran
uslijed opisane ekstruzije meniska i opisanih ganglion cisti.
U sklopu gonartroze potpuna denudacija hrskavica medijalnog kompartmenta femorotibijalnog
zgloba te stanjenje i hondromalacija 2. - 3. stupnja lateralnog kompartmenta femorotibijalnog
zgloba. Zone koštanog edema zglobnih tijela medijalnog kompartmenta femorotibijalnog zgloba.
U području hvatišta prednje križne sveze za interkondilarnu eminenciju interosalne ganglion
ciste u sklopu degenerativnih promjena.
Distenzija iliotibijalnog trakta.
Tetiva muskulusa popliteusa održana uz blaže tendinopatiju promjene. Održane su tetive PES
anserinus.
Hondromalacija 1. - 2. stupnja trohlearne i patelarne hrskavice.
Baker cista promjera 23X9 mm.
Održana je tetiva kvadricepsa i ligament patele. Umjeren izljev u koljenskom zglobu.
Atrofija m. vastus medialis i m. semimembranosus GC 2-3.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, there is focal high grade chondrosis (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at lateral aspect of medial patellar facet (about 1.7*1cm) and medial aspect of lateral patellar facet (about 1.8*1.5 cm). There is no subchondral edema. The trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is probable interstitial partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. The  posterior cruciate ligament is intact.  
 The medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of right knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion. -- Focal high grade chondrosis at the medial patellar facet (about 1.7*1cm) and lateral patellar facet (about 1.8*1.5 cm). 
 -- Probable interstitial partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.  
 -- Some amount of right knee effusion.

In the medial compartment, there is horizontal tear at the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
  
 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
  
 The patellofemoral joint, there is focal high grade chondral defect (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) with subchondral edema at the medial trochlea (about 1.5*2.5 cm). Focal cartilage fibrillation at the lateral trochlea is present (about 1.5* 1.4 cm). Focal low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the medial patellar facet (about intact7* intact7 cm). Small osteophytes are identified.  The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. There is no tibial translation. 
  
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
  
 Some amount of right knee effusion with synovitis is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  Mild patellofemoral compartmental osteoarthritis of the right knee by evidence of chondrosis, subchondral edema and osteophytes. 
  Horizontal tear at the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
  Some amount of right knee effusion with synovitis.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Sinovitis izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteración de señal difusa la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales continuos.
Rotura compleja que compromete principalmente cuerpo y cuerno anterior del menisco medial
asociado a maceración y extrusión del menisco medial con importante edema de las partes
blandas parameniscales.
Menisco lateral de morfología conservada con alteración de señal probablemente degenerativa del
cuerno anterior, sin criterios de rotura.
Avanzados cambios degenerativos femorotibiales mediales con alteración de señal difusa del
cartílago asociado a defectos parciales y amplios defectos de espesor completo del cartílago en
ambas superficies articulares, principalmente en el cóndilo femoral asociado, edema óseo reactivo
y gruesas prominencias osteofíticas. Cartílago femorotibial lateral con alteración de señal y
defectos de espesor parcial.
Cartílago patelofemoral con alteración de señal asociado a defectos de espesor parcial y algunos
de espesor total con cambios óseos reactivos en el vértice de la patela.
Engrosamiento y alteración de señal del tendón cuadricipital con cambios entesopaticos
asociados.
Engrosamiento y alteración de señal del tendón rotuliano proximal y distal.
Restantes tendones regionales de espesor y señal conservados.
Leve a moderado derrame articular con signos de sinovitis difusa principalmente en el receso
suprapatelar donde presenta fenómenos de cronicidad. Leve distensión del receso gastrocnemio
medial semimembranoso.
Planos musculares de trofismo y señal conservados.
Impresión:
Rotura compleja asociada a maceración y extrusión degenerativa del menisco medial con
acentuado edema de las partes blandas parameniscales.
Avanzados cambios degenerativos femorotibiales mediales con condropatía difusa grado 2 y
amplios defectos condrales grado 4 en ambas superficies articulares de predominio en el cóndilo
femoral.
Condropatía femorotibial lateral grado 2.
Condropatía patelofemoral grado 2 con úlceras grado 4 en el vértice de la patela.
Tendinosis y cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales. Tendinosis rotuliana proximal y distal.
Leve a moderado derrame articular con signos de sinovitis difusa
